transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-24 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramos (CTO, Harborline), Liam Chen (Full Stack Lead), Priya Nair (Security Engineer)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on time-to-first-call (Fastpass quickstart), whether Harborline should start on Redwood Hosted API or evaluate a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem), and security/compliance checklist for procurement. Customer asked for perf numbers and cost/latency tradeoffs.

Topics: Fastpass quickstart credits and TTFT; hosted vs dedicated vs private; security (SOC2, SSO, KMS); integration path (SDKs, curl, streaming); benchmark plan and next steps.

00:00 - 00:23 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for making time, i'm Maya from Redwood inference, with Daniel, our systems SE. how's everyone doing?
00:24 - 00:35 Sofia: good thanks, excited to dig in — we've got a tight window to decide which path for the holiday campaign.
00:36 - 01:05 Maya: cool, quick agenda — walk through our Fastpass quickstart (time-to-first-call), discuss hosted vs private tradeoffs, security questions, then next steps. sound good?
01:06 - 01:45 Sofia: yes — main things: we want to spin up something in a week, need to know if hosted is safe for PII-ish content, and how fast we can test.
01:46 - 02:10 Daniel: we'll cover that. to start, what does your current stack look like and expected qps?
02:11 - 03:20 Liam: we're node/python backend on GCP, nginx front, and expect 10-20 rps for vetting, spikes up to 200 qps if the campaign hits. prompts average 350 tokens but could go to 1k for long-form generation.
03:21 - 03:55 Maya: perfect — that shapes recommendations. Fastpass is our self-serve flow: sign up, get credit bundle (we'll allocate 40 free credits for a pilot), run sample requests via SDK or curl; typical TTFT (time-to-first-token) for a dev is under 15 minutes including SDK install.
03:56 - 04:35 Sofia: that low? what about model cold start and latency variability?
04:36 - 05:20 Daniel: hosted runtime has warm pools and continuous batching; median token latency for curated open models is around 50-120ms per token under small sequences, but that varies with model and seq len. for large sequences the kernel selection and kv cache matter — we can show logs.
05:21 - 06:05 Priya: on security — how is data handled in hosted mode? is there encryption-at-rest, role-based access, and audit logs? we need SOC2 evidence.
06:06 - 06:40 Maya: yes, hosted offers encryption-in-transit and at-rest, we integrate with KMS for keys in Private, and we provide audit logs and RBAC. we'll share SOC2 and network diagrams.
06:41 - 07:25 Priya: do you support SSO/SAML and SCIM for user provisioning?
07:26 - 07:50 Daniel: yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in the Console. some older transcriptions show red wood console spelled weird in docs but the product supports it — sorry, internal joke.
07:51 - 08:30 Sofia: what's the difference between Dedicated and Private? we see dedicated in other vendors described as 'reserved capacity'.
08:31 - 09:05 Maya: Dedicated = reserved GPU pools in our cloud (predictable throughput, committed monthly), Private = customer-managed VPC or on-prem control plane for stricter isolation and customer KMS/HSM integration. Dedicated is a good middle-ground if you need predictability but not full network isolation.
09:06 - 09:45 Liam: from an infra point — if we start hosted and outgrow it, how smooth is migration to Private? any SDK changes?
09:46 - 10:22 Daniel: API stays consistent — same REST/SDK surface. rollout is about networking and provisioning the private control plane; model versions/rollouts are unchanged. we can assist with data migration and routing policies.
10:23 - 11:00 Sofia: pricing question — how do we think about per-token vs reserved GPU cost? we have a narrow margin on holiday promos.
11:01 - 11:55 Maya: short answer: hosted per-token is best for quick experiments; reserved/dedicated reduces unit cost at scale. Redwood Optimize suggests batching and quant profiles to hit cost targets. we'll produce an estimate matrix with break-even points.
11:56 - 12:40 Priya: do you offer on-prem air-gapped installs? we may need that for certain vendors.
12:41 - 13:20 Daniel: we do a Private on-prem package for regulated workloads, it includes the private control plane, audit logging, and HSM/KMS integration as needed. deployment windows are longer and require infra alignment.
13:21 - 14:00 Liam: for the Fastpass we care mostly about dev velocity: how easy to run a sample inference locally and in our staging?
14:01 - 14:40 Maya: couple of clicks in Console, or npm install @redwood/inference and one sample request. streaming responses and function calls supported — dev quickstart includes sample prompts, webhook examples, and a small benchmark harness.
14:41 - 15:10 Sofia: can you show a live minimal flow? even pseudo-code?
15:11 - 17:05 Daniel: (screen share description) node example: import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY}); client.generate({model:'rw-open-v1',input:'summarize...'}).then(...). it's literally a curl post too. we'll paste examples in the quickstart email.
17:06 - 18:00 Liam: good. what about latency for streaming responses and webhooks?
18:01 - 19:10 Daniel: streaming latency is dominated by model token generation; our runtime optimizes attention kernels and kv cache to keep tail latencies down. we'll include p50/p95 examples from our model catalog; note that transcription sometimes writes 'kv-cache' as 'k v cash' in some exports, so ignore that.
19:11 - 20:00 Priya: procurement wise we need contract language for data handling, IP, and audit rights. do you have standard clauses?
20:01 - 20:35 Maya: yes we have enterprise terms and add-on compliance packs. we'll send the standard SOW and privacy sections.
20:36 - 22:05 Sofia: for the pilot, what's a realistic scope? we want up to 200 qps spikes, a couple of endpoints, and a small rerank pipeline.
22:06 - 23:10 Daniel: proposal: start hosted Fastpass with 40 credits, run the benchmark harness with your payloads, measure latency and token usage, then if the economics look right we either reserve Dedicated or provision Private depending on your security gating.
23:11 - 24:00 Liam: what's included in the benchmark harness?
24:01 - 25:10 Daniel: a lightweight harness with load patterns, batching simulation, prefix caching toggles, and quantization toggles. we'll ask you to provide typical prompts and expected throughput to tune it.
25:11 - 27:05 Priya: will the harness test SLOs with network emulation? we need to ensure real-world latencies are covered.
27:06 - 28:00 Daniel: yes, it can simulate latency and tail distribution. also can run on your VPC in Private tests if you need that environment fidelity.
28:01 - 29:00 Sofia: any blockers you see for a one-week Fastpass run?
29:01 - 29:40 Maya: none from our side; we'll provision credits and quickstart links. big blocker might be procurement sign-off for a corp card if you want more credits.
29:41 - 31:10 Liam: on integration, we prefer using our existing SDK wrappers — is rate limiting per token or per request?
31:11 - 32:00 Daniel: rate limits are per-account/route and per-token can be estimated; we'll include suggested quotas for your expected RPS.
32:01 - 33:05 Priya: encryption keys — for hosted, do you manage keys or can we bring our own?
33:06 - 33:45 Maya: hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default; Dedicated/Private allows BYOK with KMS or HSM integrations. we'll document that in the security pack.
33:46 - 35:00 Sofia: are there examples of customers who started hosted then went private? curious about migration speed.
35:01 - 36:10 Daniel: yes, we have a few case studies; migration is usually a few weeks of coordination — most friction is networking and compliance approvals on the customer side.
36:11 - 38:00 Sofia: ok, timeline — we want pilot in one week, and an internal decision in 3 weeks. is that feasible?
38:01 - 39:10 Maya: yes. next steps: we send quickstart and security docs, you run the Fastpass tests, then we reconvene with benchmark results.
39:11 - 40:40 Sofia: sounds good. Priya will own security checks. Liam will run the harness.
40:41 - 41:30 Maya: recap — I'll send quickstart, allocate 40 credits, Daniel to prep perf plan; Priya to confirm KMS requirements. expected follow-up 12/1 for deeper infra dive.
41:31 - 42:00 Meeting end / thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript quality: automated notes — some product names and acronyms may be mistranscribed (e.g., 'kv cache' sometimes 'k v cash', 'VPC' occasionally 'v p c'). There was minor crosstalk between Liam and Priya on the benchmark specifics.

Shared artifacts mentioned: Fastpass quickstart link (will be sent), security pack (SOC2, network diagrams), benchmark harness template (spreadsheet), perf estimate matrix.

Recap (short): Redwood to provide Fastpass quickstart + 40 credits and security docs; Harborline to run pilot and return perf data; follow-up dedicated deep dive scheduled early next month.
